title: Integrated Capstone: A Full Multi-Channel Campaign
summary: Learn to plan and run a cohesive multi-channel campaign that connects paid ads, organic content, SEO, and email around one clear business goal, then package it as a capstone portfolio piece.
objectives: Define a single SMART business goal and tie every channel back to it
Map the customer journey across ads, content, SEO, and email
Build a coordinated campaign calendar with consistent messaging and creative
Set up tracking with UTM parameters and channel-specific KPIs
Assemble the campaign into a professional capstone portfolio case study

quiz.q: What should every channel in an integrated campaign be tied to?
quiz.why: An integrated campaign works because every channel serves one clear, measurable goal, keeping all decisions focused.

quiz.q: Which UTM parameter identifies the type of traffic, such as cpc or email?
quiz.why: utm_medium describes the traffic type (e.g., cpc, email, organic), while utm_source names the specific platform.

quiz.q: In the customer journey, which channel set best fits the Retention stage?
quiz.why: Retention is about nurturing existing subscribers, which is the job of an email welcome series.

quiz.q: Why is consistent messaging and creative important across channels?
options: It reduces the ad budget automatically
It builds recognition and trust as users move between touchpoints
It is required by Google Analytics
quiz.why: Consistent message and visuals build recognition and trust, making conversion more likely as users cross channels.

quiz.q: Name one KPI you would use to measure the email part of the campaign.
quiz.answer: Open rate (also acceptable: click rate or conversion rate)
quiz.why: Email performance is commonly measured by open rate, click rate, and conversion rate.

quiz.q: What is the SMART criterion that ensures a goal has a deadline?
quiz.why: The 'T' in SMART stands for Time-bound, meaning the goal has a clear deadline.

body_markdown:
## Why Integrated Campaigns Matter

Real businesses rarely succeed with a single channel. A customer might see an Instagram ad, read a blog post, find you again through Google, and finally convert after an email. An **integrated multi-channel campaign** coordinates ads, organic content, SEO, and email so they reinforce one another around a single goal. This capstone proves you can think like a marketer, not just operate one tool.

## Step 1: Start With One Business Goal

Everything begins with a single, measurable objective. Use the SMART framework:

- **Specific**: Generate newsletter sign-ups for a new product launch
- **Measurable**: 500 new subscribers
- **Achievable**: based on current traffic and budget
- **Relevant**: tied to revenue or growth
- **Time-bound**: within 4 weeks

Write this as one sentence: *"Acquire 500 new email subscribers for the spring collection launch in 4 weeks on a $400 ad budget."* Every channel decision must serve this goal.

## Step 2: Map the Customer Journey

Think in stages and assign channels to each:

| Stage | Goal | Channels |
|-------|------|----------|
| Awareness | Reach new people | Paid social ads, organic posts |
| Consideration | Build interest/trust | Blog content, SEO landing page |
| Conversion | Capture the lead | Lead-gen form, opt-in offer |
| Retention | Nurture & sell | Email welcome series |

Notice how channels hand off to each other. An ad drives traffic to an SEO-optimized landing page; the page offers a lead magnet; the email series nurtures the subscriber.

## Step 3: Create a Consistent Message & Creative

Define one **core message** and one **visual identity** that appears everywhere:

- Same value proposition headline across ad, landing page, and email
- Same colors, fonts, and hero image
- Same call-to-action verb ("Get early access")

Consistency builds recognition and trust as users move between channels.

## Step 4: Build the Campaign Calendar

Sequence activity over the 4 weeks:

- **Week 1**: Publish SEO blog post + landing page; warm-up organic posts
- **Week 2**: Launch paid social ads driving to landing page
- **Week 3**: Retarget engagers; send first email to new subscribers
- **Week 4**: Final push ads + last-chance email; measure

## Step 5: Track Everything With UTMs

UTM parameters tell you which channel drove each result in Google Analytics.

`https://site.com/spring?utm_source=instagram&utm_medium=cpc&utm_campaign=spring_launch`

- **utm_source** = where (instagram, google, newsletter)
- **utm_medium** = type (cpc, organic, email)
- **utm_campaign** = which campaign (spring_launch)

Use a consistent naming convention so reports stay clean.

## Step 6: Measure With Channel KPIs

- **Ads**: CTR, CPC, cost per acquisition (CPA)
- **Content/SEO**: organic sessions, time on page, keyword ranking
- **Email**: open rate, click rate, conversion rate
- **Overall**: total subscribers vs. 500 goal, blended CPA

## Step 7: Package as a Portfolio Case Study

Document the campaign as a story: the goal, your strategy, the channel plan, screenshots of assets, the results (or projected results), and what you learned. This case study is the centerpiece of your job application — it shows end-to-end thinking.

slides.title: Integrated Capstone: A Full Multi-Channel Campaign
slides.sub: Connecting ads, content, SEO & email around one goal
slides.narration: Welcome to your capstone lesson. Today we bring together everything you've learned — paid ads, organic content, SEO, and email — into one cohesive multi-channel campaign built around a single business goal. This is the project that will anchor your portfolio.

slides.title: Why Integrate Channels?
bullets: Customers move across many touchpoints before converting
Channels reinforce each other when coordinated
One goal keeps every decision focused
Proves you think strategically, not just tactically
slides.narration: Real customers rarely buy from a single touchpoint. They might see an ad, read a blog, search on Google, and finally convert through email. Integrating channels means they reinforce one another. When everything serves one goal, your work becomes focused and far more powerful — and it shows employers you think like a strategist.

slides.title: Step 1: One SMART Goal
bullets: Example: 500 new subscribers in 4 weeks on $400
Write it as a single sentence
Every channel must serve this goal
slides.narration: Start with one clear goal using the SMART framework. For example: acquire 500 new email subscribers for a spring launch in four weeks on a 400 dollar ad budget. Write it as one sentence and pin it to the top of your plan. Every choice you make afterward must serve this goal.

slides.title: Step 2: Map the Customer Journey
slides.narration: Map your channels to journey stages. Awareness is driven by paid and organic social. Consideration is supported by blog content and an SEO-optimized landing page. Conversion happens through a lead form with an opt-in offer. Retention is handled by your email welcome series. Notice how each stage hands off to the next.

slides.title: Step 3: One Message, One Look
slides.narration: Define one core message and one visual identity that appears everywhere — the same headline, the same colors and imagery, and the same call to action. As people move from your ad to your landing page to your email, that consistency builds recognition and trust, making them more likely to convert.

slides.title: Step 4: The Campaign Calendar
bullets: Week 1: Publish blog + landing page, warm-up posts
Week 2: Launch paid ads to landing page
Week 4: Final push ads + last-chance email
slides.narration: Sequence your activity over four weeks. Week one you publish your SEO content and landing page and warm up with organic posts. Week two you launch ads. Week three you retarget engagers and send your first email. Week four is the final push and measurement. A calendar keeps the whole team coordinated.

slides.title: Step 5: Track With UTMs
slides.narration: To know what's working, tag every link with UTM parameters. Source is where the click came from, medium is the type of traffic, and campaign is the campaign name. Keep your naming consistent so your Google Analytics reports stay clean and you can compare channels fairly.

slides.title: Step 6: Measure Each Channel
bullets: Ads: CTR, CPC, cost per acquisition
Content/SEO: sessions, rankings, time on page
Email: open rate, click rate, conversions
Overall: subscribers vs. goal, blended CPA
slides.narration: Each channel has its own KPIs. For ads, watch click-through rate, cost per click, and cost per acquisition. For content and SEO, track sessions and rankings. For email, monitor open and click rates. Finally, roll it up: did you hit your 500 subscriber goal, and what was your blended cost per acquisition?

slides.title: Step 7: Build Your Portfolio Case Study
bullets: Tell the story: goal, strategy, channels
slides.narration: Finally, package everything as a case study. Tell the story of your goal, your strategy, and how each channel fit together. Include screenshots of your assets and your results or projections, and finish with what you learned. This end-to-end case study is the centerpiece of your job application.
